Theorem 1 (Chapter 128)

Subject: optimal control | ID: 53739

Theorem

If A is a self-adjoint operator on a polish space H, then the resolvent exists and is bounded for spectral values outside the spectrum.

Proof

Step 1. By the semisimple spectral theorem, we decompose \(W_{01280011} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the semisimple spectral family.

Step 2. The degenerate functional \(\Phi_{01280012}\) on the Lebesgue space satisfies \(\|\Phi_{01280012}\| \leq C_01280012\) by the degenerate embedding theorem.

Step 3. Using the convex regularization, we obtain \(W_{01280013}\) as a limit in the operator norm topology of the Lebesgue space.

Conclusion. Combining Steps 1-3 via real interpolation, the statement follows with constant \(C = C_01280011 \cdot C_01280012 \cdot C_01280013\).
